title: Microsoft Purview DLP: block Microsoft 365 Copilot responses to prompts containing sensitive data
summary: The briefing's prompt-blocking controls, default simulation state and licensing are supported by Microsoft's documentation. One minor correction remains: acknowledge that the cited education guide says administrative units are unsupported, while the feature page documents their preview rollout.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: An enforced SIT-based prompt-processing rule prevents Copilot from returning a response to a matching prompt.
claims.quote: Detects when the text entered directly into a Copilot or Cowork prompt contains chosen sensitive information types. The experience doesn't respond to the prompt.

claims.claim: Prompt blocking is admin-opt-in because the default policy only simulates until an administrator enforces it.
claims.quote: The policy is in simulation mode by default, which means it doesn't block the prompt but generates an alert and sends an email to the admin (if configured).

claims.claim: Microsoft supplies a policy called Default DLP policy - Protect sensitive M365 Copilot interactions.
claims.quote: Microsoft created a default DLP policy called **Default DLP policy - Protect sensitive M365 Copilot interactions**.

claims.claim: The default policy detects sensitive information types in user prompts.
claims.quote: The default policy detects sensitive information types (SIT) in user prompts.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default policy logs matching events while in simulation mode.
claims.quote: This means that the event will only be logged. If you want to block processing of the prompt, you must change the state of the policy to enforce mode.

claims.claim: The default policy generates an alert when it matches.
claims.quote: The policy doesn't generate any policy tips for end users, but it does generate an Alert event.

claims.claim: The default policy sends an email to the administrator if configured.
claims.quote: The policy is in simulation mode by default, which means it doesn't block the prompt but generates an alert and sends an email to the admin (if configured).

claims.claim: The default policy's administrator email is low severity.
claims.quote: It also triggers a low severity email to the admin (added in the policy).

claims.claim: DLP checks typed prompt text rather than scanning files uploaded directly into the prompt.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.claim: SIT and sensitivity-label conditions cannot be used together in the same rule.
claims.quote: You can't use both content contains sensitive info types and content contains sensitivity labels conditions in the same rule. You can create a rule for each condition in the same policy, but not in the same rule.
